clues: This city sits in the east of Finland, in a land of lakes. It stands on the north shore of a large lake, where a river flows in.
Far inland, it feels big swings in heat and cold. In July it is warmer than Dublin, but in January it is colder than Moscow.
This city was founded in 1848 by a Russian emperor, Nicholas I. He ruled the land at that time.
This is a student city, with part of a big university based here. A college for hands-on studies is here too.
This town is the capital of North Karelia. People here speak Finnish as their one tongue.
